prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2024 — Summary (within 500 words)

Framing and purpose
- It’s time for change: end 14 years of Conservative chaos that harmed family finances and public services. Restore hope, turn the page, and rebuild a country that serves working people.
- Mission-driven government: ambitious, measurable national missions delivered with fiscal responsibility, partnership with business and unions, and power pushed out to communities.

Strong foundations
- National security: unshakeable NATO commitment and UK nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review and path to 2.5% of GDP; tougher counter-espionage and counter-extremism; Martyn’s Law.
- Secure borders: create a Border Security Command, end the failing Rwanda scheme, smash smuggler gangs, hire caseworkers to clear the asylum backlog, fast-track returns, and secure a UK–EU security pact.
- Economic stability: strict fiscal rules with independent OBR oversight; no rises in NI, Income Tax rates or VAT; modernise HMRC and close loopholes (non-dom, offshore trusts, carried interest). Keep taxes on working people as low as possible.

Five missions
1) Kickstart growth: pro-business and pro-worker “securonomics”
- Industrial Strategy Council; National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd-in private investment (ports, gigafactories, steel, CCS, green hydrogen).
- Stable business taxes: cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Infrastructure: 10-year plan; faster planning for nationally significant projects; full gigabit and national 5G by 2030.
- Transport: fix roads and 1m extra potholes/year; accelerate EV rollout; bring rail into public ownership as contracts end; empower mayors on integrated transport; bus franchising and lift municipal ownership ban.
- Innovation: 10-year R&D budgets; Regulatory Innovation Office; binding rules for powerful AI models; double co-ops and mutuals; small business late-payment crackdown.
- Housing: 1.5m homes; restore targets; brownfield-first with strategic “grey belt” release; new towns; more social and affordable homes; first-time buyer protections; permanent mortgage guarantee.
- Devolution: Local Growth Plans; multi-year council funding; reform local audit.
- Immigration and skills: reduce net migration with linked skills plans; end long-term shortage list dependence.
- Work and pay: New Deal for Working People—ban exploitative zero-hours contracts, end fire-and-rehire, day-one rights, Single Enforcement Body, genuine living wage without age discrimination. Youth Guarantee (18–21).

2) Make Britain a clean energy superpower by 2030
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co-invest and deploy local power; double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCS, hydrogen, marine; extend nuclear (Hinkley, Sizewell C, SMRs); strategic gas reserve.
- No new North Sea exploration licences; tougher windfall tax; Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn) to upgrade 5m homes; carbon border adjustment; clean up rivers with tougher enforcement; restore nature; back British farmers; stronger animal welfare.

3) Take back our streets
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; crack down on antisocial behaviour (Respect Orders); new offence for assaults on shopworkers.
- Knife crime plan: mandatory interventions, ban zombie-style blades and online sales abuses; Young Futures hubs nationwide.
- Halve violence against women and girls: specialist RASSO units in every force; fast-track rape courts; stronger stalking, spiking, and policing standards; fix prisons and reduce reoffending; Hillsborough Law.

4) Break down barriers to opportunity
- 3,000 school-based nurseries; free breakfast clubs in every primary school.
- 6,500 new teachers; curriculum and assessment reform; mental health professionals in every school.
- Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; flexible Growth and Skills Levy; secure higher education; broaden access to arts and sport.
- Family security: review Universal Credit to make work pay; end Section 21 evictions; leasehold to commonhold; homelessness strategy; pensions triple lock.

5) Build an NHS fit for the future
- 40,000 extra weekly appointments; shared waiting lists; use independent capacity to cut waits.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; speed innovation and clinical trials.
- Return of the family doctor: more GPs, continuity of care, pharmacist prescribing, Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan (700,000 urgent appointments; contract reform); National Care Service with Fair Pay Agreement; 8,500 extra mental health staff; bold public health measures (smoking, youth vaping, junk-food ads).

Clean politics and a reconnected Britain
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; modernise the Commons; immediate Lords reform (end hereditary peers, retirement at 80), path to replacement; votes at 16; reset with devolved governments.
- Foreign policy: strong NATO, support Ukraine, AUKUS, clear-eyed China strategy; make Brexit work with better EU ties (trade, security, vets/MRAs); targeted trade deals (incl. India); lead a Clean Power Alliance; modernise development and restore 0.7% when fiscally possible.

All fully costed and funded within Labour’s fiscal rules. Stop the chaos. Turn the page. Rebuild a Britain that serves working people.
